knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly contrasts simple and multiple linear regression model forms?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the statement that names one X versus several X's.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Simple versus multiple is about how many explanatory variables enter the linear form. Least squares is a separate estimation criterion applied after the model is stated.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Simple: one X; multiple: several X's jointly. Least squares estimation is a separate criterion from model-form statement.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing model-form statement into least-squares estimation.

choices.label: A simple linear model has one explanatory variable; a multiple linear model has several explanatory variables entering jointly. Multiple regression can hold additional predictors simultaneously that a simple model cannot.
Simple and multiple linear models differ only in how least-squares estimates are computed; stating Y = β₀ + β₁ x + ε is already least squares.
A multiple linear model must always include interaction terms; a simple model never includes an intercept.
Simple linear regression applies only to claim frequency; multiple linear regression applies only to claim severity.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Claim severity Y with predictors age (x1) and sum insured (x2). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Write simple versus multiple forms; refuse OLS-as-form.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Simple uses one predictor; multiple uses both. Closed-form least squares is estimation, not the act of naming the model forms.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Simple: Y = β₀ + β₁ age + ε. Multiple adds β₂ sum_insured. Refuse OLS-as-form.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating least-squares estimation as finishing model-form statement.

choices.label: Simple: Y = β₀ + β₁ age + ε. Multiple: Y = β₀ + β₁ age + β₂ sum_insured + ε. Writing least-squares formulae for β̂ is estimation, not stating the simple versus multiple linear model forms.
Simple: Y = β₀ + β₁ age + β₂ sum_insured + ε. Multiple: Y = β₀ + β₁ age + ε, because multiple means more parameters in the criterion.
Both forms are Y = β̂₀ + β̂₁ x + ε where β̂ comes from minimising sum of squared residuals; stating the model is the same as clicking Fit.
Simple and multiple models are identical here because age and sum insured are both continuous; the distinction applies only when one predictor is categorical.

worked_example.title: Simple vs multiple fitted severity values
worked_example.problem_statement:
Two fitted linear models for claim severity Y (£000) are available.
Simple: Ŷ_s = 2.0 + 0.5x₁, where x₁ is age/10.
Multiple: Ŷ_m = 1.5 + 0.4x₁ + 0.3x₂, where x₂ is sum insured (£0000).
For a risk with x₁ = 4 and x₂ = 5, compute both fitted values and state which model form each equation represents.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Count the explanatory variables in each equation, then evaluate both fitted values at (4, 5).

steps.label: Identify simple vs multiple form
steps.attempt_cue: Count explanatory variables on the right-hand side of each equation.
steps.explanation: Simple linear regression has one explanatory variable. Multiple linear regression has several explanatory variables entering jointly.
steps.calculation: Ŷ_s uses only x₁ (simple); Ŷ_m uses x₁ and x₂ (multiple)
steps.result: Simple vs multiple identified by number of X's

steps.label: Evaluate the simple fit
steps.explanation: The simple model ignores x₂ even if that covariate is available.

steps.label: Evaluate the multiple fit
steps.attempt_cue: Substitute x₁ = 4 and x₂ = 5 into Ŷ_m.
steps.explanation: The multiple model adjusts the age contribution and adds the sum-insured term jointly.

worked_example.final_answer: Ŷ_s = 4.0 (£000) is simple (one X); Ŷ_m = 4.6 (£000) is multiple (two X's). Least-squares estimation is a separate step from writing the model form.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Calling Ŷ_m 'simple' because it is still linear in the parameters, or assuming the two fitted values must coincide at the same (x₁, x₂).
